purpose: Test whether the categorical calibration ceiling is explained by the rank-information constraint of binary 0/1 pairwise mismatch rather than by biological trait signal.
source: 683 novel known-truth system JSONs from workflow 37086693588 plus their frozen S3 tree geometries; no real trait values or memory rho.
mechanism: For a binary state vector, pairwise dissimilarity has only two tied ranks (match/mismatch). Spearman correlation with phylogenetic separation is therefore point-biserial correlation between separation ranks and a cut-induced mismatch indicator. This constrains attainable rho by tree geometry and class balance.
tests: For each system, record the maximum pilot median rho over the frozen OU lambda grid.
Relate maximum attainable rho to semantic class, n species, and for categorical systems the median pilot minority-state fraction at the lambda achieving maximum median rho.

For categorical systems, compute the theoretical maximum point-biserial correlation obtainable for the observed separation ranks at each possible mismatch-pair count K, ignoring whether every K is realizable by a tip bipartition; this is an optimistic upper bound.
Compare the OU-generator maximum pilot median rho with that optimistic binary-rank ceiling.
primary_prediction: Categorical systems with low calibration ceilings should have optimistic binary-rank ceilings closer to the benchmark and/or extreme class-balance constraints; if even the optimistic ceiling is below 0.15, the failure is imposed by rank geometry itself.
interpretation_guard: This is an estimator/representation geometry analysis, not evidence about categorical trait evolution.
